key_insight: Residual learning with convex projection improves machine learning-based quantum error mitigation while ensuring reconstructed density matrices are physically valid.
engineering_relevance: The framework can improve noisy-hardware bound-state simulations, with performance depending on the training states and regression model.
method: Use residual learning to reconstruct noise-mitigated quantum states.
Apply convex projection to enforce density-matrix physicality.
Evaluate Haar-random versus VQE-ansatz training states and compare against conventional ML-QEM, readout mitigation, and zero-noise extrapolation.
evidence_signal: IBM hardware tests on three- and four-qubit hypernuclear systems achieved a three-qubit energy of −0.134 MeV versus the ideal −0.135 MeV with 0.999 fidelity, and four-qubit energies of −3.014 and −3.045 MeV with fidelities of 0.995 and 0.998.
watch_item: Results are limited to small systems; scalability and robustness across different noise conditions remain to be established.
paper_title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations
